title: Trump posts AI image of penguins welcoming him to Greenland - an island without them
source_used: The Independent (full text from the fulltext folder)
key_facts: Trump posted an AI-generated image on Truth Social of a penguin colony welcoming him to Greenland, one of more than two dozen posts he made on Sunday (4 Oct 2026).
The image shows a Trump likeness before a snow-capped mountain, penguins in red, white and blue sweaters holding American flags, and 'GREENLAND' in large letters.

Greenland and the wider Arctic have no native penguin species; penguins live almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, and the Galapagos penguin, the only wild penguin north of the Equator, lives roughly 4,900 miles from Greenland.

Earlier on Sunday he posted an AI image of himself peering over the island's mountains captioned 'Hello, Greenland!'; on 27 Sep he posted an image of his face over a globe centred on Greenland captioned 'His Hemisphere.'

The posts followed a late-September security agreement among the United States, Denmark and Greenland that clears the way for an expanded US military presence while keeping Greenland within the Kingdom of Denmark.

Trump said the agreement 'gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland'; Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said it recognises the Kingdom's sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.

Trump has repeatedly voiced interest in US control of Greenland and at times suggested military force, drawing sharp condemnation from Greenlandic and European officials; polls find few Americans, and even fewer Greenlanders, in favour; about 56,000 people live there.
quote_evidence: President Donald Trump has posted an AI-generated image depicting a penguin colony welcoming him to Greenland, an Arctic island of polar bears, glaciers and fraught geopolitics - but no penguins.
One problem with the fantasy is that Greenland, and the Arctic more broadly, has no native penguin species.

The president’s penguin post was the latest in a recent string of social media messages focused on Greenland, the semiautonomous Danish territory that Trump has long sought to bring under U.S. control.
why_it_matters_hint: A light AI-image post, but on Greenland, where Trump's suggestions of using military force have drawn sharp condemnation from Greenlandic and European officials.
event_date: Sunday 4 Oct 2026 (the post); the security agreement is from late September 2026
notes: Single outlet. 'Sunday' in the article is read as 4 Oct 2026 because the report is stamped Monday 5 Oct 2026 and it dates the earlier image separately as 27 Sep. The event is a day before the window, so the entry is marked as a follow-up and the score is lowered by 1. The article does not say who made the image or whether the penguin error was deliberate.
